title: Prompt attribution trace taxonomy and dashboard sketch
body:
Overview:
This doc proposes a compact trace taxonomy and a dashboard sketch to attribute user-facing outcomes (latency, token cost, deviation from expected output) back to prompt-level constructs across the inference stack. Goal is to enable quick exploration of which prompts, prompt-turns, or prompt-fragments are driving cost/latency or causing fallback/rollouts to trigger.

Why this is needed:
- Current traces are request-first and do not consistently capture prompt composition; multi-turn prompts blur attribution.
- Ops investigations often spend time reconstructing which fragment of a prompt (system vs user vs tools) triggered a long token-generation path or a model fallback.
- We need a small, orthogonal set of span labels and attributes that allow: group-by prompt-id/turn, slice by token-range, and correlate with cache hits and quantization variants.

Goals and success signals:
- Instrumentation that lets an operator answer in 5–10 minutes: which prompt-turns contributed to a 90th-percentile token latency spike and why.
- Dashboard panels that surface top-k prompts by cost-per-response, fallback frequency, and token-latency by turn.
- Sampling rules that preserve rare but high-cost prompt patterns while controlling trace volume.

Key concepts & definitions (keep short):
- prompt-id: stable id assigned at request intake representing the logical conversation or prompt bundle.
- turn-id: integer for conversational multi-turn requests (0 = system, 1 = user, >1 subsequent).
- fragment-type: one of [system, user, tool-call, function-output, external-context].
- token-range: half-open range of generated tokens that maps to prompt fragments (e.g., 0-24, 25-79).
- generation-span: span covering model token generation phase for a token-range.
- dispatch-span: time to route request and load model keys/kvcache.
- kvcache-hit: boolean/enum {full, partial, miss} for the prefix cache check.
- fallback-path: ordered list of model variants or regions used as runtime fallbacks.

Span naming conventions (flat, human readable):
- intake.prompt (attributes: prompt-id, turn-id, fragment-type)
- dispatch.model.lookup (attributes: model, model-version, quant-level, routing-decision)
- cache.kvcheck (attributes: tenant-id, kvcache-hit, prefix-length, cache-age-sec)
- gen.token-window (attributes: token-range, model-variant, requested-seq-len, batch-id)
- fallback.switch (attributes: from-model, to-model, reason)
- emit.multipart (attributes: bytes, latency-ms, tokens-count)

Essential trace attributes (strings or small enums):
- prompt_id, turn_id, fragment_type, fragment_text_sha (short hash), token_range, model, model_variant, quantization, batch_id, tenant_id, kvcache_hit, cache_age_s, routing_decision, fallback_chain, gen_latency_ms, dispatch_latency_ms, total_response_ms, token_cost_units, sampled_by_policy

Sampling strategy (recommendation):
- Base sample: 1% of all requests (uniform).
- Stratified captures: 100% of traces where gen_latency_ms > 1000ms OR token_cost_units > threshold (tenant-weighted).
- Event-triggered: capture full trace if fallback.switch occurs or if any span reports kvcache_hit == miss AND total_response_ms > 200ms.
- Reservation: keep headroom for low-traffic tenants: maintain N traces/day per tenant to keep coverage.

Dashboard sketches (high-level panels):
1) Prompt Waterfall (left-most): selected prompt-id -> waterfall showing intake -> dispatch -> cache -> gen windows -> emit. Clickable token-range bars that filter the other panels.
2) Top prompts by cost-per-response: group by fragment_text_sha (de-dup by hash), show cost, median latency, q95 latency, fallback rate.
3) Token-range heatmap: x axis token-range buckets, y axis model-variant; color = median gen_latency_ms per bucket.
4) Fallback frequency over time: stacked area by to-model with annotations when fallback.rate spikes.
5) KV cache warmth by tenant: small multiples for tenants showing prefix-hit rate and cache_age distribution.
6) Investigator quickfilters: model-version, quantization-level, tenant-id, sampling-reason (e.g., q95, fallback).

Implementation notes & minimal instrumentation checklist (workable MVP):
- At intake: attach prompt_id and sparse fragment metadata (type, turn_id, fragment_text_sha) to the root span.
- Ensure dispatch spans carry model and routing_decision attributes.
- Emit a cache.kvcheck span with kvcache_hit and prefix_length. Avoid sending full prompt text in traces—use sha and store mapping in a secure artifact if needed.
- Generation spans should be split into token-window spans of configurable size (e.g., 32 tokens) so the waterfall shows where latency accumulates.
- Add a small per-response token_cost_units estimate in root span.

Data privacy & size controls:
- Do not put PII in attributes. Use sha for fragments and keep a TTL-limited mapping store for shas when needed for debugging.
- Token-window spans should cap stored bytes for emitted attributes.

Migration and rollout plan (2 phases):
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): instrument intake, dispatch, kvcheck, and gen.token-window (32 token windows). Add sampling rules and dashboards with synthetic probes to validate spans.
- Phase 2 (next 3 sprints): add fallback.switch traces, tenant-weights for sampling, and the de-dup hash mapping store + quicklink in dashboard to retrieve fragment text for debug (access controlled).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Best hash length for fragment_text_sha to avoid collisions vs. leakage risk? (8–12 hex chars?)
- Token-window size: 16 vs 32 tokens tradeoff between granularity and trace volume.
- How to surface aggregated prompt families (templates) vs individual prompts without storing full text?

Next steps / owners:
- Diego: prototype trace attributes in the runtime (kvcheck + token-window spans) — due 2024-12-06.
- Rinata: dashboard mockups in Grafana and a query pattern experiment — due 2024-12-13.
- Maya: sampling policy PR and rollout plan doc — due 2024-12-20.

Quick checklist before in-review signoff:
- [ ] Root span includes prompt_id and turn_id
- [ ] Cache span emitted with kvcache_hit enum
- [ ] Gen spans split into token windows and carry token_range attribute
- [ ] Sampling rules implemented in telemetry pipeline and tested with probe traces
- [ ] Dashboard panels wired to test dataset and validated with synthetic spike scenarios

Notes to reviewers: prioritize enabling investigations that combine prompt-structure and cache behavior. Keep the trace schema minimal and stable; aim for a taxonomy that supports both oncall troubleshooting and postmortem analytics without exploding trace cardinality.

End of doc.
